editorial_contributions.text:
The author shows that the discharging method [see \textit{N. Robertson}, \textit{D. Sanders}, \textit{P. Seymour} and \textit{R. Thomas}, The four-color theorem, J. Comb. Theory, Ser. B 70, 2-44 (1997; Zbl 0883.05056)] can be extended from finite planar graphs to infinite planar graphs of subexponential growth, and to those graphs that do not satisfy the strong edge isoperimetric inequality (that is, there is no positive constant \(h\) such that every finite set \(X\) of vertices has at least \(h|X|\) outgoing edges). Several applications of the method are discussed.


In particular, it is proved that every planar graph with only finitely many vertices of degree at most 5 and with subexponential growth must contain arbitrarily large finite submaps of the tessellation of the plane, or some cylinder, by equilateral triangles. Moreover, every planar graph which does not satisfy the strong edge isoperimetric inequality and which has essential minimum degree at least 3 must have infinitely many edges whose degree sum is at most 15; in particular, this holds for graphs with minimum degree at least 3 and with subexponential growth.

msc.text: Combinatorial aspects of tessellation and tiling problems
Tilings in \(2\) dimensions (aspects of discrete geometry)
